nodes.name: LLM Request Webhook
nodes.notes: POST {prompt, task_type?: simple|code|complex, max_tokens?, require_json?}. One Respond node answers every path.

nodes.name: CONFIG
nodes.notes: THE ONLY NODE YOU NEED TO EDIT. Tiers (TIERS_JSON), service URLs, budget, breaker and cache settings. See the Read Me First note and the README.

nodes.name: Routing Policy
nodes.notes: EDIT ME for routing rules: guess the task type from the prompt, which tiers (and in which order) serve each task type, default and maximum answer length, system messages, forcing JSON. Data only; checked on every request. It cannot override the caller's task_type, budgets, breakers or quality checks.

nodes.name: Validate Request
nodes.notes: Checks auth, CONFIG (including every tier in TIERS_JSON) and the request, and fills in defaults. Anything wrong is answered here with a specific message.

nodes.name: Request Id
nodes.notes: Request ids are a secure random UUID from the Crypto node. (A Code node cannot use `crypto` in current n8n.)

nodes.name: Cache Key
nodes.notes: SHA-256 of prompt + task type + max_tokens + require_json + the configured models.

nodes.name: Cache Lookup
nodes.notes: GET /cache/{key} -> 200 {body, cached_at} or 404. Any failure is treated as a miss: the cache can never fail a request.

nodes.name: Cache Verdict
nodes.notes: A hit needs a well-formed entry younger than CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (checked here) that still satisfies the request (non-empty, valid JSON when required).

nodes.name: Plan Step
nodes.notes: Entry of the loop. Picks the next tier (in TIERS_JSON order) that handles this task_type. Each pass through here is one tier; the loop ends at a success or when the tiers run out.

nodes.name: Breaker Status
nodes.notes: GET /breaker/{tier} -> {status: closed|open, next_probe_at, trip_count}.

nodes.name: Breaker Verdict
nodes.notes: closed -> go. open and cooldown over -> try to claim the single probe. open and cooling -> skip this tier. Breaker service unreachable -> fail open (and say so in the trace).

nodes.name: Claim Probe
nodes.notes: Atomic: only one request at a time wins the right to test a recovering provider.

nodes.name: Reserve Budget
nodes.notes: Atomic check-and-reserve of this call's worst-case cost. This is what makes the daily limit hard under concurrency.

nodes.name: Build Call
nodes.notes: Builds the provider-specific request from the tier definition (ollama / openai / anthropic). Retries come back here too.

nodes.name: Call Provider
nodes.notes: One node for every tier: URL, headers, body and timeout all come from the tier definition. Errors and timeouts continue as data so Assess Call can classify them.

nodes.name: Assess Call
nodes.notes: Classifies the reply. 5xx/429/timeouts/network = hard failure (retried, counts against the breaker). 401/403/404 = hard, not retried. 400-type = provider rejected this request (no breaker penalty). 2xx but empty / invalid JSON = soft failure (escalate, no breaker penalty). Computes real cost from usage.

nodes.name: Retry Delay
nodes.notes: Waits before the retry (the delay was worked out in Assess Call: exponential back-off with jitter, or the provider's Retry-After). The wait is not counted in the call's latency.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ $json.health === 'failure' ? { is_probe: $json.probe, error_message: String($json.health_error || 'failure').slice(0, 200), failure_threshold: $('CONFIG').first().json.BREAKER_FAILURE_THRESHOLD, cooldown_seconds: $('CONFIG').first().json.BREAKER_COOLDOWN_SECONDS, max_cooldown_seconds: $('CONFIG').first().json.BREAKER_MAX_COOLDOWN_SECONDS } : { is_probe: $json.probe } }}

nodes.name: Record Health
nodes.notes: Feeds the per-tier breaker: record-success or record-failure (with the probe flag). A failed probe re-opens the breaker with a longer cooldown.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ { request_id: $('Request Id').first().json.request_id, tier: $('Assess Call').last().json.tier_name, actual_usd: $('Assess Call').last().json.outcome.cost_usd } }}

nodes.name: Settle Budget
nodes.notes: Replaces the reservation with the actual cost (0 for a failed call). Retried up to 3 times: a lost settle makes the budget drift, so it is worth retrying. If it still fails the reply carries a warning and Slack is notified.

parameters.jsCode:
const S = $input.first().json;
return [{ json: { state: { next_idx: S.tier_idx + 1, attempts: [...S.state.attempts, S.record], waited_ms: S.state.waited_ms || 0 } } }];

nodes.name: Advance To Next Tier
nodes.notes: Appends this tier's result to the trace and moves on. Reached after a skip (breaker open, budget denied) or a failed attempt.

nodes.name: Finalize Success
nodes.notes: Builds the 200 reply: text, provider, cost across all attempts, usage, the attempts trace. The cache write and any alert happen after the reply.

nodes.name: Build Failure
nodes.notes: Every tier failed or was skipped: 503 with a specific reason (daily_budget_exhausted, all_providers_failed, quality_check_failed_all_tiers, all_circuits_open, budget_service_unavailable, no_eligible_tier).

nodes.name: Respond
nodes.notes: The single reply node. Every path builds {http_status, response_body} and ends here.

nodes.name: Cache Store
nodes.notes: POST /cache/{key} {body, cached_at}. Runs after the reply and failures are ignored on purpose: a missed cache write costs a little efficiency, nothing else.

nodes.name: Expand Notifications
nodes.notes: Runs AFTER the reply. Same alert key inside ALERT_COOLDOWN_SECONDS is dropped, so an outage does not flood Slack. (Throttle memory is kept by n8n with the active workflow and survives restarts.)

nodes.name: Send Notification
nodes.notes: Slack-compatible incoming webhook. Failure is ignored on purpose.

parameters.content:
## Multi-Model LLM Router
**Setup (about 10 minutes)**
1. Run the three backing services (a reference implementation is included: `node 07-multi-model-llm-router-mock-server.js`, port 4500): cache, circuit breaker, budget. Each can be switched off in CONFIG.
2. Open **CONFIG**: edit `TIERS_JSON` (your providers, cheapest first: kind `ollama`, `openai` or `anthropic`, full endpoint URL, model, prices, api_key), the service URLs, `DAILY_BUDGET_USD`, optional `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` and `ROUTER_AUTH_TOKEN`.
3. Activate, then `POST /webhook/llm/complete` with `{"prompt": "...", "task_type": "simple|code|complex", "max_tokens": 512, "require_json": false}`.

**Each request:** validate -> cache -> for each tier that handles the task: breaker gate -> reserve budget (paid tiers) -> call (retry) -> check quality -> record health -> settle cost -> accept or move on -> reply -> cache + alert.

Tiers are plain config: add, remove or reorder them without touching a node.
